title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence
summary: A preregistered experiment with 453 professionals found shorter completion times and higher assessed quality on occupational writing tasks with ChatGPT.
limitations: Short writing assignments and assessed artifacts; not long-run firm productivity.

title: Generative AI at Work
summary: A staggered workplace deployment increased customer issues resolved per hour by 15% on average, with greater benefits for less experienced workers.
limitations: One customer-support environment; assistance is embedded in a specific workflow. The published estimate differs from the earlier 14% working-paper figure.

title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier: Field Experimental Evidence of the Effects of Artificial Intelligence on Knowledge Worker Productivity and Quality
version_note: Study first circulated in 2023; linked author manuscript is a 2026 revision.
summary: An experiment with 758 consultants distinguishes tasks within the model's effective capability frontier from tasks on which AI assistance can worsen correctness.
limitations: Task-specific frontier and 2023 GPT-4; do not infer present model limitations directly.
verification_scope: author manuscript, methods and reported task contrast

summary: Developers given Copilot completed a JavaScript HTTP-server task in substantially less time; the reported reduction was 55.8%.
limitations: An isolated task and early tool; completion-conditioned estimates and uncertainty matter.

title: How much does AI impact development speed? An enterprise-based randomized controlled trial
version_note: 2024 preprint; associated ICSE 2025 Software Engineering in Practice presentation is catalogued separately.
summary: A trial with 96 Google engineers estimated approximately 21% shorter task time with internal AI features.
limitations: Wide uncertainty, one complex task, internal tooling; not an estimate for all engineering work.

title: The Effects of Generative AI on High-Skilled Work: Evidence from Three Field Experiments with Software Developers
summary: Three workplace experiments covering 4,867 developers report a pooled increase of about 26% in completed tasks following access to coding assistance.
limitations: Completed-task measures vary across firms; access, actual use, quality, and commercial value are distinct.
verification_scope: research publication page and reported pooled result

summary: Experienced maintainers took 19% longer on tasks in familiar repositories when allowed early-2025 AI tools, despite expecting and perceiving speedups.
limitations: A small, expert population and a specific model/tool vintage; not an estimate for 2026 agents.
verification_scope: primary paper abstract and linked experiment report

title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
summary: METR's follow-up describes selection and measurement problems as developers increasingly decline AI-disallowed work and operate agents concurrently.
limitations: Raw later estimates are explicitly treated as unreliable; they neither erase the original trial nor establish a new precise productivity effect.

title: Measuring the Self-Reported Impact of Early-2026 AI on Technical Worker Productivity
summary: A survey of 349 technical workers estimates perceived changes in the value of work, extending beyond time saved on fixed tasks.
limitations: Self-reported counterfactuals, selection, and unusually technical respondents; not independently measured causal uplift.

summary: A matched event study of more than 500,000 developers finds large cumulative commit effects that attenuate for projects, releases, and application usage.
limitations: Nonrandom adoption, heterogeneous tools and outcomes; cumulative event-study estimates are not daily speedup percentages.
verification_scope: current publisher abstract and revision metadata

title: Artificial Intelligence in the Firm: Bottlenecks in Software Production
version_note: Current linked version August 4, 2026; first version January 7, 2026.
summary: Firm-level adoption analysis using Jellyfish data finds increased coding activity, longer review cycles, and limited pass-through to resolved issues or epics.
limitations: Proprietary data, parallel-trends assumptions, firm-level adoption, and output proxies; insignificant effects are not proof of exactly zero benefit.
verification_scope: author PDF, abstract, introduction, review analysis and sample table

summary: Microsoft's early-2026 CLI-agent rollout is associated with roughly 24% more merged pull requests among adopters across four months.
limitations: Merged PRs are a proxy rather than value; adoption spreads through social networks and is not random.

summary: Organization-level research links AI use to individual benefits while reporting adverse associations with delivery stability and throughput in the 2024 sample.
limitations: Survey-based relationships, self-selection and organizational context; not randomized deployment effects.
verification_scope: report landing page and primary organizational interpretation

summary: The 2025 report interprets AI as an amplifier of existing organizational capabilities and weaknesses.
limitations: Organizational associations do not imply that mature practices guarantee positive outcomes for every adoption.
verification_scope: research publication page and report synthesis

summary: Discusses tensions between AI adoption, trust, verification, workflow design, and effective use across the software lifecycle.
limitations: Interpretive and practical guidance; not a new randomized productivity estimate.

summary: Vendor telemetry reports higher output alongside larger changes, review pressure, defects and incidents as AI adoption intensifies.
limitations: Selection, changing workflows, relative metrics, limited baselines, and vendor interests impede causal attribution.
verification_scope: primary report overview; numerical details require report-specific denominator checks

summary: Tracks code-change patterns, duplication and moved-code metrics across the period of expanding AI-assistant adoption.
limitations: Calendar-time association is not treatment identification; moved-code measures are not the entirety of refactoring.
verification_scope: primary report page and stated metric definitions

title: AI | 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey
summary: High reported use or planned use coexists with greater distrust than trust of AI accuracy and widespread frustration with nearly correct answers.
limitations: Opt-in survey and question-specific denominators; planned use is not adoption, and frustration is not measured net time loss.
verification_scope: AI section including exact question wording

summary: Production C++ telemetry finds distinct warning profiles, added review effort, and higher compute consumption in the studied AI-code cohort.
limitations: One enterprise and language, attribution challenges, private data; the result is not a universal defect or cost multiplier.

summary: Compares more than 500,000 Python and Java samples and identifies different defect, vulnerability and structural-complexity profiles in human and model code.
limitations: Sample construction and static classification affect comparison; simpler code is not necessarily safer or more maintainable.

summary: Static analysis of 4,442 Java assignments finds that passing functional tests does not reliably indicate broader code quality or security.
limitations: Assignments, selected models, and analyzer findings are not direct observations of production exploitation.

summary: An open-source study reports greater activity among peripheral contributors alongside added review and rework burdens for core contributors.
limitations: Contributor seniority proxies and observational adoption; review redistribution is not itself proof of lost total value.

summary: Evaluates agents across successive repository changes rather than a single static issue, making regression and maintainability central outcomes.
limitations: A benchmark environment and curated tasks; longitudinal agent evaluation is not longitudinal organizational evaluation.

summary: Coverage measurements on 4,882 agent PRs show incomplete execution of changed lines and uneven benefits from agent-written tests.
limitations: Coverage is not assertion quality; the AIDev corpus overlaps other studies and should not be counted as independent replication.

summary: Joint implementation-and-proof generation succeeds on 27 of 43 curated multi-module Lean repositories in the strongest evaluated configuration, with no complete success on the hardest cases.
limitations: Formal validity is conditional on specification; small curated benchmark and configuration-dependent result.

summary: Iterative infrastructure-code repair can regress security; changing the regression definition reduces measured affected scenarios from 13.8% to 3.3%.
limitations: Validator semantics and resource restructuring influence apparent regressions; cumulative-best metrics conceal intermediate failures.

summary: Randomized study of learning a programming library finds reduced conceptual understanding, code reading and debugging with AI assistance on average.
limitations: A small task-specific study; interaction-pattern subgroups are exploratory and not separately randomized.
verification_scope: primary abstract and preregistered design description

title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning
summary: A school mathematics trial distinguishes AI-assisted practice from unaided assessment and shows the importance of tutor guardrails for preserving learning.
limitations: Mathematics education and a specific instructional implementation; not a result for every tutor or subject.

summary: Students assisted by ChatGPT produced stronger C solutions but showed lower immediate and 48-hour recall, with no significant difference in the rate of forgetting.
limitations: 55 analyzed participants, three tasks and 48-hour follow-up; substantial physiological missingness.
verification_scope: primary abstract, full HTML methods and results

summary: Among 210 first-year OOP students, different self-reported AI-use profiles did not significantly differ in unaided assessment performance.
limitations: One course, nonrandom use and self-report; a null comparison is not equivalence or proof that pedagogy does not matter.

summary: Combines risk prediction, evidence-bounded feedback and progressive assistance using historical failed submissions from 215 students.
limitations: Retrospective prediction and message evaluation; no prospective demonstration of better unaided learning.
verification_scope: abstract and full HTML research-design section

summary: A four-day study of 21 SAP developers relates perceived cognitive load to AI use and task context; wearable measurements add limited information.
limitations: Small nonrandom sample and short observation; does not establish an overall causal increase or reduction in mental effort.

summary: A six-month survey panel reports a shift toward supervisory engineering work and growing experience-related costs despite stable perceived productivity gains.
limitations: Perceived effects, attrition and 95 matched participants; not independently timed task performance.

summary: A BNY Mellon survey with 2,989 responses and 11 interviews argues for measuring expertise, ownership and longer-run productivity alongside activity.
limitations: Self-reports within one organization; identifies constructs rather than a causal effect size.

summary: A survey of 415 practitioners maps perceived gains and shifted effort across SPACE dimensions, including review and verification costs.
limitations: Self-report and adoption differences; neither proves net losses nor measures firm-level product value.

summary: ERA iteratively searches software candidates for scorable scientific and engineering tasks, demonstrating strong empirical-software performance.
limitations: Task and evaluator design are provided by people; benchmark gains do not automatically establish a new scientific explanation.

summary: Co-Scientist generates and prioritizes research hypotheses, with selected results assessed through expert and experimental validation.
limitations: Selected biological cases and human direction; broad autonomy is not demonstrated.

summary: Robin connects literature work, hypothesis generation and analysis to selected laboratory experiments in a multi-agent discovery workflow.
limitations: A limited number of tasks and experiments; repeatable general discovery requires broader independent testing.

summary: Demonstrates an extended automated ML-research workflow and evaluation of generated work through workshop peer review.
limitations: Human selection and workshop-level assessment are not evidence of unrestricted autonomous scientific excellence.
verification_scope: journal abstract and primary publication description

summary: AlphaProof combines reinforcement learning with formal mathematical reasoning and machine-checked proofs at olympiad level.
limitations: Formalized, bounded tasks and substantial infrastructure; proof validity does not establish the value or novelty of an arbitrary question.
verification_scope: journal abstract and stated evaluation scope

summary: An evolutionary coding agent improves algorithms and infrastructure through evaluator-driven search, including selected novel mathematical procedures.
limitations: Developer white paper, selected demonstrations and human-defined evaluators; no universal research-autonomy claim follows.

summary: Automated discovery of reinforcement-learning rules yields methods competitive with hand-designed algorithms and tested in additional environments.
limitations: Search objective, environments and compute allocation are human-designed; transfer has a defined scope.

summary: Darwin Godel Machine evolves the code of coding agents using an archive and external benchmarks while retaining a foundation model as the engine.
limitations: Agent-code improvement is not autonomous selection of goals or demonstrated unbounded improvement of model intelligence.

summary: Population search over harnesses improves benchmark performance with a frozen model, treating tools, prompts and control flow as evolvable components.
limitations: Recent author-reported benchmark results require independent replication and careful train-test separation.

summary: Across 11,700 trajectories, different tool architectures alter coding-agent behavior, consistency and token consumption despite similar available actions.
limitations: Repository-issue tasks and selected actors; efficiency within this evaluation is not a firm-level productivity estimate.

summary: An end-to-end test of novel post-training research finds weak improvements relative to a withheld human method and exposes misleading result selection.
limitations: One task, few expensive runs, partly human scope assessment, and contamination in successor models.
verification_scope: full report including methods, results and limitations

summary: Five research environments expose a gap between occasional strong research results and reliable completion of long research workflows.
limitations: Small number of environments, configuration sensitivity and model vintage; workshop acceptance is distinct from main-conference acceptance.

summary: Automated researchers improve benchmarks for ten defined alignment failures, with selected transfer and behavioral auditing tests.
limitations: Unequal iterative opportunities in the human comparison, selective capability tests, and vendor-produced evidence; detected cheating trajectories were excluded.
verification_scope: technical report, evaluation protocol and caveats

summary: BootLoops connects methods across quantitative fields; domain experts redirect technically correct results toward questions with scientific significance.
limitations: Selected personal case studies and manuscripts under further verification; the author was a visiting researcher at Anthropic.

summary: A prototype internal R&D index distinguishes AI assistance, collaboration and leadership from full autonomy using a fixed task basket.
limitations: Model-rated internal documentation and approximate time weights; automation share is not research speedup or independent safety evidence.

summary: Analysis of 41.3 million papers associates AI use with individual career and output advantages but a narrower collective distribution of research topics.
limitations: Broad historical AI, not just LLMs; classifier and selection effects prevent a simple causal reading.

summary: AlphaFold structure availability appears to complement experimental biology and expand basic research on previously understudied proteins, without comparable downstream drug-development effects so far.
limitations: Domain-specific transition and observation window; predicted structures do not settle biological function or translational success.

title: Artificial intelligence and illusions of understanding in scientific research
summary: A conceptual taxonomy examines how AI's promises of productivity and objectivity can produce illusions of understanding and scientific monocultures.
limitations: A theoretical perspective rather than an estimate of the incidence or size of effects.

version_note: March 2026 revision of May 2025 working paper.
summary: Danish adoption surveys linked to administrative records reveal task reorganization but limited early average effects on earnings or recorded hours.
limitations: Denmark's institutions, short horizon and averages; null aggregate effects can coexist with occupational transitions.
verification_scope: current publisher abstract and revision metadata

summary: U.S. vacancy data show a relative decline in junior software openings and higher experience requirements after ChatGPT's release.
limitations: Vacancies and posting requirements are not headcount or direct measures of individual AI substitution.

title: Has AI Widened Employment Gaps?
summary: Candidate administrative-data study retained for verification of geographic differences in AI exposure and employment.
limitations: Current PDF retrieval timed out; citation and findings require renewed checking before use in the synthesis.

summary: U.S. payroll evidence documents disproportionate early-career employment weakness in highly AI-exposed occupations.
limitations: Exposure, age, and employment trends do not uniquely identify AI as the cause; versions and panel construction change estimates.
verification_scope: primary publication page and stated research design

title: A New Look at AI's Impact on Jobs: Firm-Level AI Spending and Workforce Adjustment
summary: Links firm AI spending and workforce records, finding stronger hiring among high-intensity adopters than among comparison firms.
limitations: Growing, larger, technical and venture-backed adopters differ before treatment; spending intensity is not a randomized intervention.

title: Canaries in the Gold Mine: Early Productivity Gains from Artificial Intelligence Creating Organization Capital
summary: Firm-level AI-skilled employment measures link recent productivity improvements to investment in durable organizational knowledge and processes.
limitations: Broader AI than chatbots, employment-based investment proxies and identification assumptions; not a license-purchase ROI estimate.

title: Generative AI and Sales Productivity: Field Experiments in Online Retail
version_note: June 29, 2026 revision; earlier title referred to firm productivity.
summary: Retail experiments across seven workflows report heterogeneous sales effects, primarily through conversion rather than basket value.
limitations: One platform, 2023-2024 interventions and short-run sales measures; not aggregate total-factor productivity.

version_note: ACM Queue uses the full subtitle; the same DOI's Crossref record uses The SPACE of Developer Productivity. Title, authors and 2021 publication year compared on 13 October 2026.
title: The SPACE of Developer Productivity: There's More to It than You Think
summary: Defines productivity through satisfaction, performance, activity, communication and collaboration, and efficiency and flow.
limitations: A measurement framework, not an AI-effect estimate; activity is one dimension rather than a complete measure.

title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
summary: Demonstrates highly accurate protein-structure prediction and establishes a foundational example of specialized AI supporting science.
limitations: Predicted structure is not equivalent to experimentally established function, dynamics or drug efficacy.

title: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
version_note: Published online December 2023; Nature volume 625 is dated 2024.
summary: FunSearch pairs language-model proposals with systematic evaluation to find new cap-set constructions and improved bin-packing heuristics.
limitations: A human-specified program representation and evaluator constrain the search; a domain result is not general research autonomy.

summary: Fall 2025 U.S. enrollments fall in traditional Computer and Information Science while Data Science and Analytics grow.
limitations: Enrollment shifts do not identify AI-driven motivation and can include changes in program labels and international flows.

title: UK higher education student numbers fall for second year in a row
summary: UK 2024/25 official data show growth in Computing and AI despite a decline in total student numbers.
limitations: Different period and classification from U.S. figures; a geographic contrast rather than direct refutation.
verification_scope: official statistical release as indexed by the publisher

summary: Organizes recurring methodological mistakes in claims about AI-assisted coding and the measurement of productivity.
limitations: Critical expert commentary, not an independent outcome study.

summary: Proposes that cheaper implementation shifts engineering value toward judgment and responsibility, potentially hollowing out intermediate roles.
limitations: An argued hypothesis, not a measured labor-market result or established forecast.

summary: Personal experience with agent-generated applications raises questions about retaining a mental model and building a sustainable development career.
limitations: A selected experience and polemical argument; cannot establish prevalence or causation.

summary: Discusses reported limits on Uber's coding-agent spending and the mismatch between token consumption and demonstrable customer value.
limitations: Commentary on reporting; not an audited cost-benefit analysis of Uber.
